findings: The aggregator builds partialProviders from successful providers when another provider fails or remains pending. Consequently, search-health interprets surviving providers as degraded while rejected providers are not identified.

The aggregator also discards providers' own performance.partialProviders and performance.providerTimeouts metadata; when all providers resolve, it returns partialProviders as empty regardless of nested degradation.

Bounded recommendation: derive degraded identities from failed or unfinished providers and preserve nested degradation metadata, deduplicating identifiers while retaining usable results. Extend aggregator regression coverage for rejection with a surviving provider, timeout, nested partial results, and fully successful discovery.

Existing aggregator tests verify surviving results after rejection but do not assert degraded-provider identity. Search-health unions partialProviders and providerTimeouts and uses them to determine partial coverage and retry recommendations, establishing the user-visible impact.
